thread:
incident-bot: 🔔 ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for prod-eu streaming ingest route (p99 = 2.8s > SLO 0.9s). Auto-pager sent.

anna: I'm on it, joining bridge. Any customer-facing errors reported?

luis: A couple of escalations — customers reporting timeouts on long streaming sessions, no data loss so far.

jay: Looking at live dashboard — spike aligns with KV cache miss rate jumping from ~2% to ~38% around 23:04 UTC.

mike: Reproduced high tail in staging with long-context sessions. Suspect eviction storm on prefix cache.

anna: Quick checks — any deploys to runtime or cache config in the last 30m? @jay

jay: No service deploys. There was an autoscale policy tweak for dedicated pools at 22:58. Investigating routing and cache logs.

obs-bot: Top p99 traces (sampling):
```
trace_id: 0x7a3f... service=runtime exec_time=2.71s step=kv-fetch miss=true
trace_id: 0x9b4c... service=runtime exec_time=3.05s step=kernel-compile
```

jay: Kernel-compile spikes shown in traces — looks like many requests hit cold paths because KV miss forced fallback and expensive compile.

anna: Mitigation options: 1) partial route shift to eu-standby, 2) increase KV cache TTL, 3) force warmup of popular prefixes. Mike, can you run a small route shift?

mike: Initiating 10% route shift to eu-standby now. Watching p99 for 60s.

(60s later)

mike: Route shift in progress — p99 for shifted subset down from 2.8s -> 1.2s. Overall p99 still ~1.9s.

jay: I'm preparing a small hotfix: raise KV prefetch threshold and enable prefetch for top-100 prefixes. Will roll to canary.

luis: Notifying affected customers that we're actively mitigating; ETA ~15m for visible improvement.

zoe: Ping me with SLA exposure details so I can prep comms and support brief.

jay: Canary deployed to 5% of capacity — canary p99 ~0.78s, memory and evictions look nominal.

anna: If canary holds, roll to 50% then 100%. Watch memory and eviction rates during roll.

mike: Rolling to 50% now — monitoring.

(2m later)

mike: 50% roll complete. Overall p99 trending: 2.8s -> 0.95s. Back within SLO window, but we'll keep the page open until stable.

jay: Follow-ups: deep KV eviction analysis, add prefix-hotness telemetry, and create runbook steps to auto-warm top prefixes after cache rebuilds. I'll own the postmortem.

luis: I'll update customers and the status page with mitigation summary.

incident-bot: Incident severity reduced to sev-2. Postmortem assigned to eng-runtime. Closing urgent paging; keep incident channel open for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
